No later Gentleman Bastard novel, short story, unpublished future volume, adaptation, game, or author interview is story canon for this pass.

coverage_rule: Include the five named active Gentlemen Bastards (Locke, Jean, Calo, Galdo, and Bug), their named formative mentor Father Chains, the named Camorri criminal ruler and his daughter (Capa Barsavi and Nazca), and the two named plot-driving coup antagonists (the Grey King and the Falconer). This ten-person cohort covers the gang, its mentor, the Secret Peace's incumbent leadership, and the opposing conspiracy. Minor named nobles, thieves, guards, priests, unnamed victims, collective gangs/orders, and all non-person entities are omitted.
omissions: Red Seas Under Red Skies, The Republic of Thieves, later short fiction, any unpublished/future Gentleman Bastard work, and every continuation of the characters after this novel
All adaptations, games, comics, interviews, author annotations, maps/bonus material, translations, audio performances, and later/reformatted editions as independent continuity evidence
Minor named Camorri figures, nobility, city officials, priests, thieves, mercenaries, servants, guards, and victims outside the stated ten-person coverage rule
The Gentlemen Bastards, capae, the Secret Peace, the city of Camorr, confidence games, gods/religions, Bondsmagi, Elderglass, artifacts, temples, ships, and magic as character nodes
uncertainties: The novel alternates its principal confidence-game action with chronological interludes from Locke's childhood and gang formation. Every record identifies its part/interlude locator and does not flatten aliases or relationships across those time layers.

Disguises, cover identities, plans, and testimony are purposeful deceptions in the text. Alias fields distinguish labels rather than treating every asserted role or confidence-game premise as independently true.

The primary reading witness is copyright-controlled and loan-limited. The author’s official opening sample is UK-spelled and may differ in typography from the declared US hardcover; chapter/part labels are therefore preferred over page claims. No extended quotation is reproduced.

The novel includes child endangerment, gang violence, torture, murder, threats, sexualized coercion, class exploitation, and strong language. These are recorded descriptively, without endorsement or sensationalism.
Camorri, Vadran, Therin, and religious/magical terms are fictional constructs. No term receives a normalized archetype mapping or a real-world cultural/religious equivalence.
evidence_basis: Claim-level records use the controlled primary novel scan by exact part/chapter/interlude locator. Scott Lynch's official excerpt provides primary opening evidence; the official books page distinguishes Book I from later sequence titles; Penguin Random House provides publisher/format metadata and an authorized Chapter One excerpt. No fan wiki or Wikipedia is used.
